question.text:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a_2}$, and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine if $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $x_1 \cdot x_2$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b} = x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2}.$

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix} . \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} -3x_1+x_2 = -5 \\ -3x_1+x_2 = 7 \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,}\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -3 & 1 & -5 \\ -3 & 1 & 7 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 - R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -3 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 12 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0x_1 + 0x_2 = 12,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b}. \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that $\mathbf{b}$ does not lie in $\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}.$

question.text:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a_2}$, $\mathbf{a_3}$, and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine if $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2, \mathbf{a}_3 \}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $x_1 \cdot x_2 \cdot x_3$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b} = x_1 \mathbf{a}_1+x_2 \mathbf{a}_2 + x_3 \mathbf{a}_3.$

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 3 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{a_3}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ -9 \\ 13 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 10 \\ -16 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2}, \mathbf{a_3} \}$ if there exist $x_1$, $x_2$ and $x_3$ such that \begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} +x_3 \mathbf{a_3}&= \mathbf{b} \\ x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 3 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + x_3 \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ -9 \\ 13 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 10 \\ -16 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1-3x_3 = 5 \\ 3x_1+x_2-9x_3= 10 \\ -4x_1+13x_3 = -16 \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align} &\phantom{\sim\,\,} \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -3 & 5 \\ 3 & 1 & -9 & 10 \\ -4 & 0 & 13 & -16 \end{array} \right] & R_2 &:=R_2 - 3 R_1 \\ &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -5 \\ -4 & 0 & 13 & -16 \end{array} \right] & R_3 &:=R_3+4R_1 \\ &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

Now, we have the system

\[ \begin{cases} x_1-3x_3 = 5 \\ x_2 = -5 \\ x_3 = 4. \end{cases} \]

From the third equation, we get $x_3=4.$ Substituting into the first equation gives

\[ x_1-3(4) = 5 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1=17. \]

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2, \mathbf{a}_3 \}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $\mathbf{b}$ as a linear combination of $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a}_2$ and $\mathbf{a}_3\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 17 \mathbf{a_1} + (-5) \mathbf{a_2} + 4 \mathbf{a_3} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] 17 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix} + (-5) \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + 4 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ -9 \\ 13 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 10 \\ -16 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Finally, $x_1 \cdot x_2 \cdot x_3 = 17 \cdot (-5) \cdot 4 = -340.$

question.text:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a_2}$, and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine if $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $x_1 \cdot x_2$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b} = x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2}.$

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{a}_1+x_2 \mathbf{a}_2 &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 3 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+3x_2 = 2 \\ 3x_1+10x_2 = 4 \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,}\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 10 & 4 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 - 3R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

Now, we have the system

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+3x_2 = 2 \\ x_2 = -2. \end{cases} \]

From the second equation, we get $x_2=-2.$ Substituting into the first equation gives

\[ x_1+3(-2) = 2 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1=8. \]

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $\mathbf{b}$ as a linear combination of $\mathbf{a}_1$ and $\mathbf{a}_2\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 8 \mathbf{a_1} + (-2) \mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] 8 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} + (-2) \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Finally, $x_1 \cdot x_2 = 8 \cdot (-2) = -16.$

question.text: Determine if the vector $\mathbf{u}$ lies on the plane $\Pi : \mathbf{r}=s \mathbf{b} + t \mathbf{c}$, $t,s \in \mathbb{R}$, where $\mathbf{b}=\left\langle -1, 4, -5 \right\rangle$, $\mathbf{c} = \left\langle 3, -9, 15 \right\rangle$, and $\mathbf{u}= \langle 2, -2, 11 \rangle.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s \cdot t$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{u}=s \mathbf{b} + t \mathbf{c}.$
question.explanation:
By definition, $\mathbf{u} \in \Pi$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

\begin{align*} s \mathbf{b}+t \mathbf{c} &= \mathbf{u} \\[5pt] s \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 4 \\ -5 \end{bmatrix} + t \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -9 \\ 15 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -2 \\ 11 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} -s+3t= 2 \\ 4s-9t = -2\\ -5s+15t = 11 \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,} \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 4 & -9 & -2 \\ -5 & 15 & 11 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2+4R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \\ -5 & 15 & 11 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 - 5R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0x_1 + 0x_2 = 1,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of $s$ and $t$ such that

\begin{align*} s \mathbf{b}+t \mathbf{c} = \mathbf{u}. \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that $\mathbf{u}$ does not lie on the plane $\Pi.$

question.text:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a_2}$, and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine if $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $x_1 \cdot x_2$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b} = x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2}.$

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -5 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -17 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{a}_1+x_2 \mathbf{a}_2 &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -3 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -5 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -17 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+3x_2 = 3 \\ -3x_1-5x_2 = -17 \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,}\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & 3 \\ -3 & -5 & -17 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 + 3R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & -8 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= \dfrac{1}{4} R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

Now, we have the system

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+3x_2 = 3 \\ x_2 = -2. \end{cases} \]

From the second equation, we get $x_2=-2.$ Substituting into the first equation gives

\[ x_1+3(-2) = 3 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1=9. \]

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $\mathbf{b}$ as a linear combination of $\mathbf{a}_1$ and $\mathbf{a}_2\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 9 \mathbf{a_1} + (-2) \mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] 9 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} + (-2) \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -5 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -17 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Finally, $x_1 \cdot x_2 = 9 \cdot (-2) = -18.$
